'''Nal Yeshu''' was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that occupied the fourth [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] position within the [[Y'Toub system/Legends|Y'Toub system]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] region. The planet lay on the junction of four [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] called the [[Oktos Route]], the [[Ootmian Pabol/Legends|''Ootmian Pabol'']], the [[Pabol Hutta/Legends|''Pabol Hutta'']], and the [[Shag Pabol/Legends|''Shag Pabol'']]. During the [[Galactic War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3642 BBY]], a secret [[Unidentified Imperial listening post|listening post]] that was used by the Empire was [[Attack on Nal Yeshu|destroyed]] by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] hired by the Republic.

==Description==
Nal Yeshu was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] with two [[Moon/Legends|moons]] that was located within the [[Y'Toub system/Legends|Y'Toub system]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] region. The planet occupied the fourth [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] position around its [[Star/Legends|star]], [[Y'Toub]], and lay on the junction of four [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] called the [[Oktos Route]], the [[Ootmian Pabol/Legends|''Ootmian Pabol'']], the [[Pabol Hutta/Legends|''Pabol Hutta'']], and the [[Shag Pabol/Legends|''Shag Pabol'']]. The Oktos Route connected Nal Yeshu to the planet of [[Kleeva]] while the ''Ootmian Pabol'' linked the planet to the world of [[Du Hutta]]. In addition to that, the routes of ''Pabol Hutta'' and ''Shag Pabol'' joined Nal Yeshu with the planets of [[Hosko]] and [[Rorak 4]], respectively.<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
The territory surrounding Nal Yeshu had come under the control of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Species/Legends|species]] approximately by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]]<ref name="EGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and was considered well-[[Scout/Legends|explored]] by [[8000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> During the [[Galactic War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]]<ref name="SWTOR" /> in [[3642 BBY]],<ref name="date">{{TOR_dates|2}}</ref> Nal Yeshu housed a secret [[Unidentified Imperial listening post|listening post]] used by the Empire. That year, local [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] that had been hired by the Republic [[Attack on Nal Yeshu|attacked]] the [[Listening post/Legends|listening post]], causing it to sever all communications with the Empire. All that remained of the post after the attack was smoking ruins.<ref name="SWTOR" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
An individual affiliated with the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Empire visited Nal Yeshu at that [[Time/Legends|time]] in order to discover the fate of the listening post, and they also uncovered evidence that indicated the perpetrator of the attack.<ref name="SWTOR" />
{{Endgame}}
The local population average of the region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] containing Nal Yeshu around the year [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]] ranged from 10 billion to 100 billion.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Nal Yeshu was first pictured in the entry for the planet of [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]] in [[The Holonet]] feature of the official website for ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''&mdash;a [[2011]] [[Star Wars video games|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[BioWare]]. Nal Yeshu was depicted in a schematic of the Y'Toub system. Since its establishment in [[2008]], ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} website has gone through a number of changes, resulting in the removal of some of the features and images that were originally located there, including the aforementioned schematic. Nal Yeshu's name was first revealed in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''&mdash;a reference book co-authored by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]], and published on [[August 18]], [[2009]]&mdash;which placed the planet in grid square S-12. The planet was later mentioned again in ''[[Star Wars]]: The Old Republic'', in which it was used as a possible location for Imperial players to assign their companions on individual quests.
